headline: MarketWatch says Nvidia's shares are holding up better than Broadcom's and Oracle's amid worries about AI debt, because Nvidia's earnings forecasts keep rising.
score_reason: Pool score 5 kept: an opinion column read only second-hand, with figures that match other coverage.
importance_line: What changed is that credit worries about AI spending are hitting heavily indebted AI builders' shares harder than Nvidia's, which matters first to savers whose funds hold Oracle, Broadcom or Nvidia, then to lenders pricing the debt, and the doubt is that this is a columnist's reading of share and default-insurance data, relayed second-hand, and wider spreads do not mean a default is near.
summary: In an opinion column of 10 Oct 2026, relayed by International Business Times Singapore, MarketWatch finds that Oracle's shares have fallen more than 40% since 2 June and Broadcom's about 25%, while Nvidia's forward earnings estimates have risen more than 30% (against more than 20% for Broadcom and about 14% for Oracle), which cushioned the fall in Nvidia's valuation. Separate coverage cited in the same account puts Oracle's credit default swap spread (the price of insuring its debt against default) at a record 261 basis points, against 80 to 87 for Nvidia; wider spreads show investors want more compensation for risk but do not mean a default is near.
